transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (BlueCrest Head of ML), Laura Gomez (BlueCrest Platform Engineer), Tom Reynolds (BlueCrest CTO)

Summary (auto): Short discovery to understand BlueCrest's migration goals from OpenAI to a Dedicated/private inference setup. Main themes: eval parity, cost/latency trade-offs, compatibility with vLLM/TGI stack, security (VPC/KMS), and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro: i'm Alex, AE at Redwood. with me is Priya, our SE. could you do quick intros?
[00:12] Samir Patel: yeah hi i'm Samir, head of ml at BlueCrest. we own the product models and evals.
[00:18] Laura Gomez: Laura, platform eng, we run infra, kubernetes, proxy, cost controls.
[00:22] Tom Reynolds: Tom, CTO, i'm here for security/compliance and timeline.
[00:30] Alex Kim: awesome. quick agenda: discovery of current stack, constraints, success metrics, then discussion on Redwood Dedicated vs Private, followed by next steps. sound good?
[00:36] Tom Reynolds: yes

---
Context / current stack
[00:45] Samir: currently we use OpenAI's API for most production text gen. for some large-batch offline jobs we run TGI on our k8s backed by vLLM for faster throughput, especially with 8-bit quant. cost is getting high on the OpenAI calls plus we want more control over routing and latency.
[01:10] Priya Shah: when you say TGI/vLLM, are those fully self-hosted in prod or more experiments?
[01:15] Samir: mix. we have a few services on vLLM in staging; prod is still OpenAI for reliability reasons. we need parity on outputs before moving anything.
[01:25] Laura: also, data residency is becoming a requirement for a European customer segment; we need VPC and KMS support, audit logs for compliance.

---
Requirements & success criteria
[01:40] Alex Kim: good, so key items i'm hearing: 1) output parity with OpenAI for your prompt sets, 2) cost reduction per token, 3) predictable latency/SLOs for customer-facing APIs, 4) security (SOC2, VPC, KMS). Anything else?
[01:57] Samir: also support for function calling / structured outputs and streaming. and ability to pin model versions for rollouts.
[02:05] Priya Shah: one clarification — is the biggest driver cost or control?
[02:09] Samir: both. cost triggers the initiative but control (on-prem options, audit) is key for enterprise deals.

---
Discussion: Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted
[02:20] Alex Kim: Redwood Hosted is easiest to get started, but seems like you want isolation and control. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with capacity guarantees and is still managed by Redwood. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives the most control but takes longer to set up. you mentioned EU residency — that pushes toward Dedicated in region or Private.
[02:45] Tom Reynolds: timeline wise we're targeting a pilot in 6 weeks if possible. is that feasible for Dedicated?
[02:52] Priya Shah: Dedicated pilot is definitely doable in that window; Private (on-prem) usually takes longer because of network/ops onsite integration.
[03:05] Laura: for Dedicated, what's the SLA and ops model? we need runbook access, incident contacts, and tracing hooks into our observability stack.
[03:13] Alex Kim: we provide an SLA for latency and uptime on Dedicated tiers, exportable traces into your tracing backend, and RBAC/SSO. we'll share the SLA sheet.

---
Compatibility & eval parity
[03:30] Samir: biggest technical question: can Redwood run the same families/models such that our outputs match OpenAI's? we do a lot of fingerprinting and hallucination checks.
[03:40] Priya Shah: short answer: yes for many open models. longer answer: parity depends on the exact model weights and sampling parameters. we can run parity evals on Dedicated with the models you use; quantization and kernel differences can slightly change outputs.
[03:55] Samir: what about function calling and tool-calling compat? we rely on structured json output and stop tokens.
[04:02] Priya Shah: we support function-calling like semantics and structured output modes; sometimes the transcription of tool names or schema keys gets fuzzy in auto transcripts but functionally it's supported.
[04:12] Tom Reynolds: you mentioned quantization affecting output — how big is the delta? for our case even small semantic shifts matter.
[04:20] Priya Shah: it varies. int8 quantization on certain archs can change token probabilities; we mitigate with calibration, KV cache strategies, and re-rolling evals across quant modes. recommended path is: run parity using your prompt set across full-fp and quantized profiles, look for regression, then choose a config that meets your quality threshold.
[04:40] Samir: can you run vLLM backend plugins or is that orthogonal?
[04:45] Alex Kim: Redwood's runtime is GPU-optimized and has its own batching and KV cache; we can integrate patterns similar to vLLM but we don't require you to bring vLLM. for customers already running vLLM, we sometimes port their configs and replicate the batching + memory patterns.

---
Performance & cost discussion
[05:05] Laura: our baseline 95th latency for OpenAI is ~220ms for 512 token responses; cost per 1M tokens is $X (Samir, can you confirm?)
[05:15] Samir: yeah our blended OpenAI bill is roughly $1,200 per 1M tokens (internal blended with some larger-context calls) and we'd like to see at least 30-40% unit cost reduction.
[05:25] Priya Shah: Dedicated typically yields better unit economics because of reserved capacity and tuning (batching/caching). we also provide Optimize recommendations (batch sizes, quant profiles) to hit cost targets.
[05:35] Tom Reynolds: latency targets for customer-facing calls are <250ms P95. can you achieve that on Dedicated?
[05:42] Priya Shah: yes, with partitioned pools and low-latency routing we can meet that for many model sizes; we can run a benchmark with your prompt set to validate.

---
Security / compliance
[05:58] Tom Reynolds: we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, per-request audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. also IP/data residency for EU customers.
[06:08] Alex Kim: Redwood has SOC2, SAML, audit logs, and we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments; Dedicated can offer isolated pools in region. we'll attach the security pack.
[06:18] Laura: for Dedicated is network traffic egress controlled? we need VPC peering or private endpoints.
[06:23] Priya Shah: yes, Dedicated supports private networking options and VPC peering; Private/on-prem includes more fine-grained network control.

---
Objections / concerns raised
[06:35] Samir: main risk is drift vs OpenAI outputs and the time to validate. also concern about developer ergonomics — we use the OpenAI spec widely.
[06:44] Priya Shah: we support OpenAI-compatible APIs for many endpoints; function calling semantics and the OpenAI shape are supported to reduce friction. there will be some mapping for model names though.
[06:55] Tom Reynolds: cost of switching — e.g., integration work, QA, and eval time.
[07:00] Alex Kim: agree. that's why we propose a narrow pilot: a handful of endpoints, parity eval, and a canary rollout. reduces migration risk.

---
References shared
[07:10] Priya Shah: i'll share a sample parity runbook, Dedicated pricing tiers, and an ops-onboarding checklist. (links: https://redwood.example/pricing/dedicated, https://redwood.example/security-pack)
[07:20] Samir: we'll share the prompt set and eval rubric via the internal s3 link (Samir to provide).

---
Recap & next steps
[07:30] Alex Kim: recap — Redwood to: 1) send Dedicated pricing and SLA (Alex) 2) run parity eval on Dedicated with your prompt set (Priya) 3) share parity runbook and onboarding checklist (Priya) 4) BlueCrest to share prompts and baseline metrics (Samir).
[07:48] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. target dates?
[07:53] Alex Kim: pricing by 11/24, ask to get prompt set by 11/22, parity results by 11/28, and then we schedule technical deep dive for private deployment early december.

---

[08:14] Priya Shah: yes per-route and per-version, canary rollouts supported.
